record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Which polynomials on C^2 are projectively isotrivial, in the sense that all of their generic fibers have isomorphic smooth projective models?

evidence.quote: By the way, is it possible to describe those polynomials on C2 which are projectively isotrivial in the sense that their generic ﬁbres all have isomorphic smooth projective models?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Call a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[x,y]$ projectively isotrivial if there is a Zariski-open subset $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ such that for every $c \in U$ the fiber $f^{-1}(c) \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ is a smooth affine curve whose smooth projective completion is isomorphic, as an abstract smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{C}$, to a fixed curve $\overline{C}$ (independent of $c \in U$). Give a description (classification) of all projectively isotrivial polynomials $f \in \mathbb{C}[x,y]$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a complete classification of projectively isotrivial polynomials on $\mathbb{C}^2$. There is a rich literature on isotrivial and birationally isotrivial fibrations of surfaces, but no explicit resolution of this specific descriptive problem could be confirmed, so the status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Birationally isotrivial fiber spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fiber spaces in which all fibers are birational to a fixed variety; related but does not classify projectively isotrivial polynomials on C^2.
status_evidence.claim: Related general theory exists but does not provide a classification answering the question.

status_evidence.title: Projective varieties covered by isotrivial families
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses isotrivial families on projective varieties, not specifically polynomials on the affine plane.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the affine-plane case is given.
